P518248.project_abstract: Rehabilitation of the Kajeke dam and the associated irrigation perimeter Gihanga III, combined with related capacity building and agricultural value chain development.

P518954.project_abstract: Mauritania's agriculture sector encompasses irrigable land, livestock, and coastal fisheries but remains significantly below its productive potential. Smallholder farmers, agribusinesses, and rural entrepreneurs are constrained by fragmented value chains, weak post-harvest and cold-chain infrastructure, limited access to finance, and an underdeveloped enabling environment. The Project development objective (PDO) is to increase the productivity and market integration of selected agricultural value chains in Mauritania, with a focus on smallholder farmers, women, and youth, and to mobilize private investment in agribusiness.To increase productivity and market integration, the Project targets two priority value chains notably horticulture and fodder with complementary support to livestock, dairy, and aquaculture. Investments in climate-smart production practices and producer organization address productivity constraints; investments in post-harvest and cold-chain infrastructure and integrated aquaculture systems address quality and loss reduction; and strengthened linkages to the Tiguint agri-food platform, the [Systeme de Veille du Marche/Market Surveillance System: SVM], and urban and export markets address market access constraints. Together, these investments are expected to reduce post-harvest losses, improve compliance with quality and food safety standards, and connect producers more effectively to higher-value domestic and export markets.Consistent with the PDO's focus on smallholder farmers, women, and youth, the Project embeds gender- and youth-sensitive design across all components, targeting these groups as producers, entrepreneurs, and market participants rather than through standalone activities. This ensures that productivity and market integration gains are broadly shared rather than concentrated among a narrow set of larger or better-connected producers.To mobilize private investment in agribusiness, the Project will deploy guarantee mechanisms, agricultural insurance, and matching grants to de-risk agribusiness investment, leveraging One-WBG instruments (IBRD, IFC, and MIGA) to catalyze private finance at scale in value chains where investment risk is currently a binding constraint. This is complemented by support to the agricultural finance ecosystem and to policy and regulatory reforms that strengthen the broader enabling environment for agribusiness, ensuring de-risking instruments operate within an improving systemic context rather than substituting for it.Effective implementation is supported through dedicated project coordination, monitoring and evaluation, and knowledge management systems. A Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) will enable rapid reallocation of resources in response to eligible crises, protecting development gains against climate and other shocks.
P518954.borrower: Ministry Of economic affairs and development
P518954.impagency: Ministry of Agriculture and Food Soverignity
P518954.project_name: Mauritania Agriculture Value Chains Development Project

P517123.project_abstract: This phase establishes the institutional architecture and human capital needed to sustain South Africa's transformed freight logistics system. Years of underinvestment have created acute skills shortages across rail operations, track maintenance, signaling, and logistics management. To address this, the phase will establish a Logistics Centre of Excellence, modernizing training through simulation-based learning, digital operations labs, and modular curricula. Programs will be developed with universities, TVET institutions, and employers, combining pre-service training with apprenticeships and structured work-based learning. Targeted outreach will attract women and youth, while upskilling and reskilling programs will support workers adapting to automation, open-access operations, and new business models. In parallel, the phase will operationalize the Transport Economic Regulator (TER), developing open-access tariff frameworks, network access rules, and dispute resolution procedures, while strengthening the Department of Transport's capacity to oversee a competitive, privately-participated sector. The phase also supports transforming Transnet Engineering into a Rolling Stock Leasing Company (ROSCO) through a public-private partnership, reducing Transnet's debt while accelerating rail market liberalization and fleet modernization.
P517123.project_name: South Africa Rail & Ports Sector Governance and Skills Development

P515398.project_abstract: The proposed Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Kenya (ASCENT Kenya) is aligned with Government of Kenya’s electrification and clean cooking goals as stipulated in the Vision 2030, Kenya National Energy Policy 2025 - 2034, and Kenya National Electrification Strategy (KNES) (2025-2030), which aim to achieve universal electricity access and access to clean cooking by 2030. It is further aligned to Kenya’s Fourth Medium Term Plan (2023 – 2027) under Vision 2030 and its strategy for job creation by supporting macro and small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) through credit facilitation, technology access and market linkages; and raising agricultural productivity through improved value chains.The project will increase energy access and access to clean and efficient energy solutions for productive uses leveraging solar energy  for households, commercial, and industrial users, and public institutions in rural, peri-urban and urban areas through clean energy solutions including refrigeration and air conditioning, and to support value chains that increase productivity and create jobs.The Project will adopt an inter-sectoral to collaborate with other sectors and leverage synergies across World Bank-financed activities particularly including in Agriculture, Education, Health, Transport and Water sectors.
P515398.impagency: Rural Electrification and Renewable Energy Corporation,The Ministry of Energy and Petroleum
P515398.project_name: Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Kenya

P515197.project_abstract: The Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA) aims to enhance the sustainability, reliability, and inclusivity of Cameroon’s electricity sector, aligning with national development strategies and energy recovery plans. Through three phases, the MPA will address sector-wide inefficiencies and lay the groundwork for long-term improvements via infrastructure investments, governance reforms, and capacity building. This initiative supports Cameroon’s ambition to become a regional energy hub and contributes to World Bank objectives like poverty reduction, climate resilience, and private sector growth.The first phase of the MPA will serve as a platform for operational experimentation and institutional learning. This will particularly be the case in areas such as utility turnaround strategies, transmission line financing schemes, DRE deployment models, and new performance-based financing instruments. The design includes targeted technical assistance, capacity-building, and monitoring systems that will generate data and insights to inform strategic adjustments for phases two and three.
P515197.impagency: Société Nationale de Transport de l'Électricité (SONATREL),Agence de l'Electrification Rurale (AER),Ministry of Water and Energy,SOCADEL (Société Camerounaise d’Électricité)
P515197.project_name: Cameroon Electricity Sector Turnaround and Access Program Phase 1

P508320.project_abstract: The proposed Central African Power Pool Regional Interconnection and Access (CAPP-RIA) Program is a Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA) operation that aims to expand regional electricity trade and increase access to electricity services in the Central African region. Supporting the establishment of a regional electricity market will enhance energy security, reduce costs of electricity supply and improve the resilience of the energy system. CAPP-RIA comprises two phases that focus on three thematic pillars: 1) strengthening institutional capacity, 2) expanding electricity access, and 3) augmenting regional integration. Over the next 10 years, CAPP-RIA will support regional integration in Central Africa through investments and technical assistance in developing the regional transmission network, reinforcing and expanding national and cross-border transmission and distribution systems, and strengthening the enabling institutional and regulatory environment for efficient power trade. Phase 1 includes preparing and implementing on-grid access projects in the Central African Republic (CAR), Gabon, Republic of Congo, and Cameroon, as well as Medium-Voltage (MV) cross-border projects. It also involves pre-investment studies for High-Voltage (HV) interconnections. For Phase 1, the CAPP Secretariat will be the implementing agency for the technical assistance aspects of the project whilst the national power utilities in the involved countries shall execute the on-grid access and MV cross-border investments.
P508320.borrower: Central African Republic,Gabon,Republic of Cameroon,Republic of Congo
P508320.impagency: CAPP Secretariat,Ministre du Développement de I'Energie et des Ressources Hydrauliques,Ministry of Water and Energy,Ministère de l'Acces Universel à l'Eau et à l'Energie
P508320.project_name: Central African Power Pool Regional Interconnection and Access (CAPP-RIA) - Phase 1

P517776.project_abstract: The proposed Ghana Financing Inclusive and Sustainable Oil Palm Project (FINPALM) Project aims to support more and better jobs through inclusive and sustainable investments in Ghana’s oil palm value chain by expanding access to long-term patient capital and addressing key constraints to private investment. The operation will deploy catalytic financing mechanisms to de-risk early-stage investments, mobilize private capital, and enable the development of inclusive, sustainable, and commercially viable plantation, processing, and value chain assets.FINPALM will combine catalytic financing and targeted enabling interventions to improve investment readiness, including support for FPIC-compliant land access and structuring, smallholder integration through financially viable anchor-outgrower models, and strengthened value chain coordination and market linkages. It will also support the resolution of key policy and market constraints, including regulatory issues and market distortions that undermine incentives for domestic production and investment. The operation contributes to implementation of the Ghana Agriconnect Compact by advancing the Compact's objectives for sector transformation through private investment mobilization, value addition, access to finance, and employment creation.
P517776.project_name: Ghana Financing Inclusive and Sustainable Oil Palm Project

P519431.project_abstract: Purpose: This Phase 1 of a ten-year Multiphase Programmatic Approach combines large investments in transport, sanitation, and urban upgrading with regulatory reforms in urban governance and land, to mobilize private sector investments and create jobs for a more inclusive and competitive Abidjan. It is delivered through five target zones, where these investments and reforms are concentrated and coordinated. Phase 1 is financed through Investment Project Financing and is designed as a platform to attract co-financing.Context: Greater Abidjan generates over 40 percent of national gross domestic product, but congestion costs 1.2 billion US dollars a year, 30 percent of residents live in informal settlements, and no authority governs the metropolitan area.Scope: The operation envisages integrated investments across five strategic zones of Greater Abidjan, combining : (i) climate resilient urban infrastructure, including flood management, drainage and sanitation; (ii) urban mobility, encompassing BRT extensions, multimodal interchange/parking hubs, e-mobility, and active mobility solutions; (iii) strategic connectivity and logistics, including priority road connections, regional corridors such as Abidjan–Lagos, urban logistics facilities and port/industrial areas; (iv) urban upgrading, including improvements to informal settlements, public spaces and green urban infrastructure; and (v) institutional strengthening and policy reforms to enhance metropolitan governance, integrated urban planning, land management and lagoon transport operations.Alignement with CPF, PND, and Greater Abidjan masterplan: This operation is aligned with the Country Partnership Framework for Cote d'Ivoire (FY2023-FY2027), which focuses on improving human capital, reducing disparities and building resilience, and creating private sector jobs as it contributes through flood resilience, affordable and safer mobility, upgrading of informal settlements, and investments and reforms that mobilize private capital and jobs. It also supports the national development plan 2026-2030, notably Pillar 5 on strategic infrastructure and regional economic hubs, ecological transition, climate resilience and circular economy, by enhancing the competitivity and inclusivity of Abidjan as a metropolitan economic hubs. Finally, it also supports the Greater Abidjan Master Plan (SDUGA) 2040, the Government's long-term spatial framework, by translating it into prioritized, coordinated investments in transport, drainage, sanitation and land, and by building the institutions to plan, finance and implement them across the ministries and local authorities.
P519431.borrower: Ministère des Finances et du Budget
P519431.impagency: Ministère de l’Hydraulique, de l’Assainissement et de la Salubrité,Ministère de l’Urbanisme, du Logement et du Cadre de Vie,Ministère des Infrastructures et de l'Entretien Routier,Ministère des Transports et des Affaires Maritimes
P519431.project_name: Integrated Mobility and Urban Development for Sustainable Growth in Abidjan MPA - Phase 1

P519503.project_abstract: The Lesotho Skills Acceleration Project will increase skilled graduates and workers for priority value chains and strengthen the skills system’s responsiveness to labor-market demand. Energy, requiring about 18,000 jobs annually over the 10-year investment period, and water, requiring skills in purification, treatment, utility operations, and leakage control, were selected with agriculture because major investments will sustain demand. Agribusiness, tourism, and manufacturing were prioritized to leverage industry-designed, demand-led programs to accelerate graduates’ employment.Aligned with the Set4Jobs MPA, the objective will be achieved through three mutually reinforcing areas:1. Prepare youth for better jobs. This includes developing and upgrading accredited programs at basic, intermediate, and advanced levels; strengthening pre-vocational secondary schools; expanding training and trade-testing capacity in underserved areas; integrating ICT and AI into delivery; and embedding Industrial Advisory Committees in institutional governance and programs delivery.2. Increasing employment opportunities in select value chains. Support will include Skills Development Fund grants, apprenticeships, internships, on-the-job training, employer and community-based platforms, and Recognition of Prior Learning. NEET youth, young women, orphans, and vulnerable children will receive targeted support for business formalization, incubation, licensing and business development. The project will incentivize proven private-sector and Youth Resource Center programs, using the National Information System for Social Assistance for targeting.3. Build industry-led skills systems. This will institutionalize private-sector engagement; update the TVET Act and related policies; introduce performance-based financing; establish a digital skills management information system with tracer-study capabilities; align occupational standards, curricula, assessment, and certification with market demand; and strengthen instructor training and deployment. Where feasible, reforms will be informed by evidence from surveys conducted with IFC developed tools such as VITAE and D4TEP, and findings from the ongoing Skills for Jobs Policy Review pilot.

P519832.project_abstract: The Ethiopia Urban E-Mobility Ecosystems Transformation Project (UBEET) MPA is designed as a 2-phase vertical MPA with an overall financing amount of US$600m, with Phase 1 at an estimated US$285m and Phase 2 at an estimated US$315m. Of this, IDA finances a total share of the UBEET MPA of US$150m , with the current UBEET Phase 1 at US$70m, and UBEET Phase 2 at US$80m. The UBEET MPA aims to accelerate public transport electrification in Addis Ababa and other Ethiopian cities. Building on Ethiopia's leadership on emobility, the project will support the development of viable business models for e-buses, e-midibuses and e-minibuses, support the modernization of the paratransit sector, build charging and energy infrastructure, promote local manufacturing, assembly, jobs and skills, support sustainable public transport maintenance and operations, and strengthen the policy, institutional and regulatory frameworks for the emobility ecosystem. It is designed to be implemented in collaboration with IFC, MIGA, other development partners and local banks. A US$5 million preparation grant has already been approved in May 2026 to support project preparation.
P519832.impagency: Addis Ababa City Transport Bureau,Ministry of Logistics
P519832.project_name: Ethiopia Urban Emobility Ecosystem Transformation Project (UBEET) Phase 1

P520060.project_abstract: Regional DARES Phase 2 will include Guinea and Cote d’Ivoire and will build on the approach established under Phase 1. The operation will support DRE solutions to connect households and businesses, promote productive uses of electricity, power critical public services through Energy-as-a-Service (EaaS), and provide technical assistance and capacity building to government institutions. The regional approach will aggregate markets and harmonize key implementation processes across countries, creating economies of scale, reducing transaction costs, and making DRE markets more attractive to private operators and investors. Private sector engagement will be at the core of the operation. A technology-agnostic approach will allow private developers to propose least-cost DRE solutions adapted to local needs, supported through Results-Based Financing (RBF). Deployment will combine developer-driven Unsolicited Proposals (USPs) with Minimum Subsidy Tenders (MSTs) for areas requiring competitive subsidy allocation, helping mobilize private capital while expanding electricity access efficiently and at scale.  In Phase 2, the project will provide: (i) electricity access to 6,300,000 people and 114,800 businesses; (ii) 31,070 electricity connections for productive uses of energy; and (iii) electricity access to 1,580 public institutions, including 700 schools and 880 health centers, enabling them to deliver essential public services.
P520060.borrower: Republic of Côte d'Ivoire,Republic of Guinea
P520060.project_name: Regional Program for Distributed Access Through Renewable Energy Solutions Phase 2

P518731.project_abstract: Chad's education crisis is proving to be a constraint to private sector growth, jobs, and economic transformation. The economy remains anchored in hydrocarbons, with oil accounting for around 14 percent of GDP and nearly two-thirds of exports. Yet two decades of oil production and private investment have not generated broad-based transformation, a strong domestic supplier base, or a deep pool of skilled Chadian workers and jobs. Chad's experience demonstrates that natural resources and investment alone will not create jobs at scale unless domestic workers and firms develop the capabilities required to participate in productive value chains.The World Bank Group's renewed focus on jobs provides an opportunity to address this constraint differently. Roughly half of primary school-aged children remain outside the education system, while learning outcomes in literacy and mathematics are critically low. At the same time, Chad's skills system remains weakly connected to the productive sectors expected to drive growth. The result is a broken capabilities pipeline: too few young people acquire strong foundational skills; too few successfully transition into market-relevant technical training; and firms face a limited pool of workers they can train, certify, and employ.  Chad will not be able to diversify beyond hydrocarbons, deepen domestic participation in oil and related value chains, or expand employment in agribusiness, energy, infrastructure and other productive sectors if large numbers of young people enter working age without the basic capabilities required to learn and work productively.The proposed national operation, to be implemented by the Ministry of National Education, Bilingualism, and Civic Promotion and the Ministry of Higher Education, Scientific Research and Vocational Training, aims to establish a clear line of sight from foundational learning to jobs and address this pipeline from foundational learning through industry-led skills development. At the basic education level, the project would focus on ensuring that young Chadians acquire measurable literacy, numeracy, problem-solving, digital, and socio-emotional capabilities required for further training. All aspects of a typical education sector system strengthening operation, such as, teacher professionalization, learning recovery, and expanded access would be organized around these outcomes.  To the extent possible, private and non-state providers could be competitively contracted and paid against independently verified learning gains, particularly where public delivery has struggled to reach excluded learners.Beyond basic education, the operation would support a fundamentally different model of TVET and skills development, in which industry is not simply consulted on curricula but plays a leading role in deciding what training is financed and delivered. In hydrocarbons and energy, infrastructure, agribusiness, logistics, and other sectors with employment potential, and where private firms and industry associations abound, the private sector would identify priority occupations and competency gaps, co-design occupational standards, and directly deliver or commission training. Public financing would increasingly follow demonstrated demand from industry rather than predetermined training supply.  The aim would be to establish industry-led Skills Compacts in selected sectors.  Under these compacts, firms or industry consortia would commit to co-financing, providing equipment or instructors, offering workplace training, and assessing competencies. In return, the operation would competitively finance training through qualified public or private providers.  As part of this compact, lead firms in the hydrocarbon, energy, and infrastructure sectors will be incentivized to open existing corporate training capacity to local suppliers and young Chadians, helping build transferable capabilities in areas such as industrial electricity, welding, mechanical maintenance, instrumentation, logistics, and equipment maintenance. This would ensure that training is not narrowly focused on today's oil jobs but supports the demands of Chad's most sophisticated industries to build transferable capabilities across the wider economy.Working as a One World Bank Group, IFC would identify workforce constraints affecting existing investors and prospective investments, convene anchor firms and industry consortia, and assess opportunities to expand commercially viable private education and training providers. IFC engagement with firms could help convert investment pipelines into concrete occupational and skills demand, while World Bank financing could address the equity and market failures that prevent poor and excluded young people from accessing industry-linked training.
P518731.borrower: Ministry of Finances, Budget, Economy, Plan and International Cooperation
P518731.impagency: Ministry of Higher Education, Scientific Research and Vocational Training,Ministry of National Education, Bilingualism, and Civic Promotion
P518731.project_name: Chad: Enhancing Foundational Learning and Skills for Jobs Project

P517997.project_abstract: The proposed operation supports the Government of Madagascar’s agriculture objectives to accelerate agribusiness transformation, job creation, and food and nutrition security through a results-based approach. The program focuses on strengthening domestic agrifood value chains—particularly staples and high-potential sectors—by improving market access, crowding in private investment, and addressing key structural constraints along production, aggregation, processing, and market linkages.The PforR will finance a government-led program centered on policy and regulatory reforms such as quality standards, agricultural financing mechanisms, subsidy rationalization, and competition, and the strengthening of core public systems  such as extension, market information, digital platforms, and sector coordination. Disbursements will be linked to the achievement of measurable results, including increased volumes of domestic agrifood products marketed through structured value chains, improved access to markets for farmers and agribusiness SMEs, and the creation of more and better jobs. By aligning incentives toward performance, strengthening institutional capacity, and improving the enabling environment for private sector participation, the program aims to shift the sector toward more productive, market-oriented, and resilient agribusiness systems.
P517997.borrower: Ministry of Economy and Finance (MINISTERE DE L'ECONOMIE ET DES FINANCES)
P517997.impagency: Direction de la Coordination et du Suivi-Evaluation des Programmes - DCSEP (Ministre de l'Economie et Finance),Ministry of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty (MINISTRE DE L'AGRICULTURE ET DE LA SOUVERAINETE ALIMENTAIRE)

P519331.project_abstract: The proposed operation constitutes Phase 2 of the restructured Mozambique Power for Jobs, Growth, and Regional Integration (Moz Power) Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA), formerly the Green Energy Corridors MPA. The operation will finance the construction of a new 400 kV transmission corridor between Pambarra, Inchope, and Matambo (PIMA), associated substation investments, and support technical assistance activities.The operation represents a transformational investment that will strengthen national energy security, increase transmission capacity, improve system reliability, facilitate future hydropower and renewable energy development, and support increased regional power trade within the Southern African Power Pool (SAPP). The operation is expected to be implemented by EDM with support from MIREME and will be co-financed alongside development partners. The restructuring will transform the MPA into the World Bank Group's integrated platform for supporting Mozambique's emergence as a regional energy hub, bringing together transmission, hydropower development, regional power trade, and private capital mobilization within a single programmatic framework. Phase 2 will support construction of the approximately 750 km Pambarra-Inchope-Matambo 400 kV transmission backbone, and substation investments, as well as provision of technical assistance. The investment will complete the integration of Mozambique's central and southern power systems, strengthen energy security, reduce constraints on power transfers, and enable more efficient use and evacuation of existing generation, including Cahora Bassa (HCB). By reducing reliance on external wheeling and imports, the backbone is expected to generate annual savings to EDM of over US$20 million. It will also provide the backbone infrastructure for future generation, including Mphanda Nkuwa (MNK), and for expanded regional power trade. The project will be co-financed by the World Bank, the European Union (EU), and the European Investment Bank (EIB). The World Bank will finance a segment of the line, the owner’s engineer, and technical assistance, while the EU and EIB will pay for the other segment of the line, the new and expanded substations, and complementary technical assistance. Although focused on transmission infrastructure, Phase 2 is a foundational investment for the broader Moz Power MPA. By creating a national power system and connecting generation resources to domestic demand centers and regional markets, it will enable future hydropower development, including the 1,500 MW MNK hydropower project, and reinforce Mozambique's position as a major supplier within the Southern African Power Pool. PIMA is required independently of MNK but provides critical transmission capacity for its development and future power evacuation.The operation will be processed together with the introduction of changes to the MPA. The revised program architecture will include Phase 3, which will support MNK as the hydropower component of the MPA through the proposed IDA guarantee and associated technical assistance, alongside support for existing hydropower assets. Additional future phases may support further transmission investments, regional interconnections, and independent transmission initiatives as sector needs evolve. The MPA will provide the common framework for coordinated IDA, IFC, and MIGA engagement under one objective, coordinated delivery arrangements, and contribute to a shared results framework.The operation is aligned with the FY26-31 Mozambique Country Partnership Framework (CPF). It directly supports Pillar 2: Foundational Infrastructure, specifically Outcome 3: Improved Energy Access and Powered Economic Corridors, by strengthening the national transmission backbone and contributing to the CPF indicator on new high-voltage power transmission capacity linking the central and southern economic corridors. The operation will reinforce grid integration, support Mozambique's objective of universal electricity access, and provide critical infrastructure to power domestic and regional economic corridors.The operation also supports the CPF's emphasis on leveraging electricity exports, mobilizing private investment in the energy sector, and developing a reinforced transmission backbone linking the north, central, and southern systems as a foundation for economic transformation, private sector growth, and job creation.
P519331.project_name: Mozambique Power for Jobs, Growth, and Regional Integration (Moz Power) - Phase 2

P519064.project_abstract: The proposed Nigeria INFRAGROW Project is an innovative infrastructure financing and de-risking platform anchored and co-developed by the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority (NSIA). It is conceived as a targeted institutional intervention to address the structural constraints that impede infrastructure investment across the project lifecycle: from upstream project preparation and structuring, through financial close, to long-term financing and debt service. The Platform seeks to bridge Nigeria’s infrastructure-finance intermediation gap by deploying a complementary suite of catalytic financing and de-risking instruments that mobilize domestic and international capital into bankable infrastructure assets. These functions will be delivered through four ring-fenced, independently governed subsidiaries, each targeting a distinct market failure while operating within an integrated financing architecture:1. Project Preparation Facility (PPF): The Platform's upstream project-development engine. The PPF finances the pre-investment work required to to transform infrastructure concepts into technically feasible, economically justified, commercially viable, and bankable investment opportunities. This includes detailed feasibility studies, transaction structuring and risk allocation, and procurement support through financial close. This is the stage at which project economics are tested, avoidable risks are mitigated, controllable risks are allocated to the parties best able to manage them, and financing and de-risking requirements are identified.2. Viability Gap Fund (VGF): The VGF provides targeted financial support to priority economic and social infrastructure projects that are economically justified but cannot achieve commercial viability under affordable user tariffs or fiscally sustainable public payments. Under the proposed endowment model, the VGF would preserve its capital base and finance viability-gap support primarily from investment returns, enabling the sustained mobilization of private capital and support for successive generations of projects. 3. Risk Capital Facility (RCF): The RCF provides catalytic equity and quasi-equity financing, including mezzanine instruments, to commercially viable infrastructure projects facing shortages of junior risk-bearing capital. Through minority equity investments and subordinated, patient capital, the RCF strengthens project capitalization, improves financial structuring, and mobilizes additional private investment. 4. Credit Guarantee Vehicle (CGV): The credit-enhancement arm of the Group, providing guarantees and related risk-mitigation instruments to unlock long-term infrastructure financing. Through its suite of three products (windows), the CGV will give investors and lenders a choice of risk-mitigation instruments to de-risk projects and improve bankability: (i) a window capitalized by NSIA equity, an IBRD/IDA loan, and other DFI participation, covering specified commercial credit and debt-service default risks; (ii) a window backed by an IDA Payment Guarantee and offering protection against public-offtaker payment risks; and (iii) a PRI window, backed by MIGA's political risk insurance, protecting eligible foreign equity and shareholder loans against specified non-commercial risks. By mitigating credit risks and enhancing the creditworthiness of eligible instruments, the CGV supports longer financing tenors, reduces borrowing costs, and mobilizes domestic capital from banks, pension funds, insurers, and other institutional investors.Beyond these financing instruments, the proposed Project would address address policy, regulatory, and institutional capacity constraints that undermine private investment in infrastructure. This would include targeted reforms and capacity-building support to strengthen the ability of relevant public-sector institutions to identify, prepare, appraise, procure, implement, and oversee PPP projects, including the assessment, monitoring, and management of associated fiscal commitments and contingent liabilities. In this respect, INFRAGROW is closely aligned with the World Bank Group’s Nigeria Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for FY26–FY32, particularly its emphasis on mobilizing private capital for infrastructure and supporting more and better jobs through private sector-led growth.As founding shareholder, NSIA is expected to provide an indicative US$200 million equity commitment to the INFRAGROW Group HoldCo, establishing the Platform's domestic anchor capital and demonstrating strong sponsor commitment and alignment. The proposed Platform presents an opportunity to operationalize a coordinated One WBG approach, drawing on the complementary investment, financing, and risk-mitigation capabilities of the WB, IFC, and MIGA. Under the proposed arrangement, IFC is envisaged as a co-anchor investor, providing catalytic risk-bearing capital to strengthen the Platform's capitalization, reinforce corporate governance and E&S standards, and mobilize additional private equity and debt financing. This would be complemented by tailored instruments under the WBG Guarantee Platform to mitigate residual risks that constrain private participation. These include an IDA guarantee to address liquidity disruptions arising from public-sector payment contractual obligations, and MIGA PRI to protect eligible foreign equity investments and shareholder loans against specified non-commercial risks. Together, these interventions would strengthen the Platform's institutional and financial capacity, enhance investor confidence, and support the mobilization of long-term private capital into priority infrastructure investments.
P519064.project_name: Nigeria Infrastructure Financing and De-Risking Platform for Growth and Jobs (INFRAGROW) Project

P510702.project_abstract: The proposed REFI project supports the Government of Cote d’Ivoire in restoring the financial sustainability of the electricity sector and accelerating the energy transition. It includes an IBRD Loan Guarantee of up to EUR [622] million to help refinance arrears and short-term debt, thereby creating fiscal space and restoring investor and lender confidence and to enable investment in grid-connected solar generation and battery storage. The project also includes a EUR [17] million IBRD Loan to provide technical support to CI-Energies for effective project implementation. REFI is part of a broader energy sector recovery and reform program under the Government’s Energy Compact and the World Bank Group’s engagement.The project includes three components:Component 1: Arrears clearance and short-term debt refinancing -- supported by IBRD guarantee-backed commercial financing to clear payment arrears to IPPs and gas suppliers and refinance short-term liabilities.Component 2: Green investments in renewable energy and battery energy storage systems -- supported by IBRD guarantee-backed commercial financing for two 120 MWp solar PV plants with 120 MWh battery storage and associated transmission, to expand clean energy and grid reliability.Component 3: Technical assistance and capacity building -- supported by IBRD loan to provide institutional and technical support to CI-Energies for the preparation, procurement, and implementation of solar and storage investments.
P510702.project_name: Côte d'Ivoire Renewable Energy & Financial Stability Initiative

P513960.project_abstract: The Mpatamanga hydroelectric power project is a 358.5 MW power plant situated on the Shire River in southern Malawi. The Mpatamanga project is a Build-Own-Operate-Transfer (BOOT). The draft Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) has a duration of 35 years, with five years construction and 30 years of operation. The PPA has a capacity-based tariff, and the payment obligation is guaranteed by the Malawian government. Total estimated power production when commissioned is 1,544 GWh/year.
P513960.impagency: Ministry of Energy, Republic of Malawi

P514522.project_abstract: The Project Development Objective of the Mpumalanga Jobs and Energy Transition (MJET) Project is to improve employment pathways for at‑risk communities in four municipalities hosting five coal‑fired power plants (CFPPs) scheduled for decommissioning under the Repowering Energy Systems for Energy Transition (RESET) MPA. MJET (Phase 1b of the RESET MPA) comprises three interlinked components designed to address the socio‑economic impacts of the retirement of five CFPPs under Phase 3 of the MPA and to generate sustainable economic opportunities linked to the energy transition in the four host Local Municipalities (LMs).Component 1: Socio‑Economic Infrastructure and Employability Pathways supports employment pathways for communities affected by CFPP closures by combining short‑term jobs with labor‑intensive, community‑based infrastructure that stimulates local economic activity. The component will profile and support at‑risk workers through a worker registry, provide career counseling and employment intermediation services, and finance small‑scale, labor‑intensive socio‑economic infrastructure in areas surrounding the five power stations (across four municipalities). Component 2: Enterprise Development, and Skills Enhancement supports at‑risk communities in the four target municipalities through skills development and support for SMMEs and cooperatives aligned with emerging local economic opportunities, with an initial focus on the energy and agriculture sectors. Activities include: (i) place‑based economic opportunity mapping and stakeholder mobilization; (ii) upgrading and operationalizing an existing training institute in Nkangala District Municipality to deliver accredited, industry‑aligned training and structured workplace‑based learning; (iii) establishment of a community enterprise incubation and support platform; and (iv) a business accelerator to support high‑potential SMEs and cooperatives with growth and market integration.Component 3: Sustainable Energy Access and Services aims to scale up investments in energy efficiency (EE), distributed energy resources (DER), and off‑grid solutions in the four affected municipalities to reduce energy costs, improve reliability, and expand energy access while supporting local economic development. This component will be delivered through three subcomponents: (i) technical assistance for energy planning, project preparation, and capacity strengthening; (ii) scaling up energy efficiency investments in municipal infrastructure; and (iii) expanding energy access and resilience for vulnerable households.

P518972.project_abstract: The proposed project is fully aligned with and operationalizes the Government of Rwanda’s AgriConnect Compact, a country-level initiative structured around seven pillars to accelerate Rwanda's transition to a modern, market-led agrifood system. MADAP is a multi-sectoral investment operation focused on improving competitiveness of the value chains that have been prioritized by the AgriConnect Compact, including maize, rice, avocado, chili, Irish potato, dairy, poultry, and piggery, through an integrated combination of productive alliance facilitation, climate-resilient irrigation infrastructure, and agricultural finance de-risking mechanisms. The project is anchored in Rwanda's Vision 2050 and the Second National Strategy for Transformation (NST 2), and is designed to crowd in private sector investment while strengthening the policy and institutional enabling environment for agribusiness development.

P512158.project_abstract: The Central Africa Regional Digital Integration Program (CARDIP) is a multi-phase programmatic approach (MPA) that aims to accelerate digital transformation and deepen regional integration by addressing key constraints in connectivity, digital adoption, and fragmented markets across Central Africa. Its Program Development Objective is to increase affordable internet access and use of digital services, and integrate digital markets in participating countries. To achieve this, CARDIP supports coordinated investments in resilient and affordable broadband infrastructure—including cross-border connectivity—while strengthening policy and regulatory frameworks, data governance, and cybersecurity to enable trusted data exchange and interoperability. Crucially, the program places a strong emphasis on driving digital adoption by expanding the availability and usability of high-impact digital services, scaling Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) such as digital ID, payments, and data exchange platforms, and investing in digital skills, awareness, and user-centric design to ensure that individuals, businesses, and governments not only have access to connectivity but are able and incentivized to use digital technologies productively. The program places strong emphasis on inclusion, ensuring that underserved populations—particularly women, youth, rural communities, and refugees and host communities—can access connectivity, build relevant skills, and translate digital access into tangible economic opportunities and improved access to services.

P519068.project_abstract: UgIFT II is Phase 1 PforR operation of  the multi-phase programmatic approach (MPA) operation. It is embedded in Uganda's Fourth National Development Plan (NDP IV, FY2025/26–FY2029/30) programs for human capital development, productive employment, and strengthened public institutions, and directly supports implementation of the government's Intergovernmental Fiscal Transfer Reforms. The UGIFT II supports in the Public Financial Reform Strategy  (PFMRS) by strengthening the link between resources, institutional performance, and service-delivery outcomes at the subnational level, building on earlier gains under UGIFT I. The program will focus on five result areas including : (a)  Getting human resource to work by ensuring that staff at subnational level are in the right place and performing effectively; (b) Enabling services to run by ensuring  that operational inputs and resources are reaching the point of  service delivery in a timely manner and quantity; (c) Making infrastructure last through maintaining functionality of  service delivery facilities and closing access gaps; (d) Managing to perform by ensuring that the management information systems are integrated and provide key data for effective accountability and performance; and (e) Getting the financing right by ensuring  that adequate resources  are provided and linked to performance at the service delivery level. The program will also support increasing local economic development to ensure job creation and own source revenue enhancement.

P517139.project_abstract: The proposed Infrastructure Financing Guarantee Facility (IFGF) of Egypt (IFGFE) operation will support the establishment and capitalization of a dedicated infrastructure guarantee platform aimed at mobilizing private capital for strategic infrastructure investments in Egypt. Building on international experience and adapted to the Egyptian context, the IFGFE will operate as a commercially managed non-bank financial special purpose vehicle providing payment guarantees, termination guarantees, and debt service guarantees to mitigate off-taker payment and debt servicing risks for infrastructure projects.The operation seeks to address structural constraints in Egypt’s infrastructure financing market, including limited availability of long-term local currency financing, elevated financing costs, and growing constraints on sovereign guarantees and contingent liabilities. The facility will initially focus on sectors with significant investment pipelines and private participation potential, including renewable energy, transmission infrastructure, water desalination, wastewater treatment, waste-to-energy, and private-to-private renewable energy projects.The operation will finance the capitalization and operationalization of the IFGFE, support the development of a pipeline of bankable infrastructure projects, and provide technical assistance for sector reforms, institutional strengthening, and market development. The facility is expected to mobilize domestic and international private capital, including commercial banks, institutional investors, Development Finance Institutions, and GCC investors, while reducing reliance on sovereign guarantees and supporting fiscal sustainability.
